summary: Elevated 5xx wave correlated with control-plane heartbeat flood and certificate rotation during morning traffic ramp
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC customers (notably Fathom Analytics on a dedicated pool) began observing a sustained increase in 5xx responses from the hosted API. Impact: ~18% of requests for the affected tenant failed with 502/503/504 over a 45-minute window during morning ramp. Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated GPU pool, api-gateway fronting multiple serving-runtimes. Initial signal: Grafana alert for 5xx-rate > 8% for tenant route.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route high-concurrency small-payload streaming and embedding requests to the tenant on prod-us-east
2) Observe increased TLS renegotiations on api-gateway and a rise in connection half-open sockets
3) After ~10-15 minutes low-level runtime watchdog resets start appearing and upstreams return 502s/503s
4) Failure pattern is amplified if the control-plane performs a certificate rotation or bursts of heartbeat messages coincide with traffic ramp
logs_snippets: [2026-03-10T08:14:03Z] apigw: TLS renegotiation count increased: +12/s for tenant-42-route
[2026-03-10T08:17:09Z] runtime-serve-3: watchdog: GPU warmup timeout, nvml reset triggered
[2026-03-10T08:18:02Z] auth-proxy: upstream read error: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-10T08:20:41Z] apigw: 502 returned to client, upstream unhealthy (half-open socket backlog=312)
[2026-03-10T08:25:12Z] control-plane: cert-rotation job started for dedicated-pool-42 (batch=8)
investigation_notes: Initial triage: alerting showed 5xx spike started ~2 minutes after an automated control-plane healthcheck sweep and coincident with a cert-rotation job for the dedicated pool.

Correlation: TLS renegotiation rate tracked to a burst of control-plane heartbeats plus parallel cert-rotate operations that caused a flurry of short-lived TCP connections while runtimes were completing background model prefetchs.
Hypothesis 1: cert rotation + increased handshake rate exhausted accept queue on the runtime side causing socket churn and subsequent GPU watchdog timeouts.

Hypothesis 2: control-plane heartbeat fanout amplified to api-gateway when route weights were briefly rebalanced, causing accept queue pressure at ingress proxies and leading to runtime threadpool starvation.
Metric evidence: accept_queue_depth and halfopen_sockets correlated with 5xx spikes. Runtime GC/gpu-reset logs line up with top of spike. No single model code regression identified.
Customer impact: Fathom reported retries and timeouts in their ingestion pipeline; latency-sensitive clients observed tail latencies rise from ~120ms to >2s before failures increased.
Cross-links: Slack thread #support-incident-133337 captured early cross-team triage. See slack.com/archives/C01SUPPORT/p167847...
mitigation_and_resolution: Short-term mitigation: throttled control-plane heartbeat fanout and paused the cert-rotation job for dedicated-pool-42. Applied a temporary apigw backpressure setting to limit concurrent handshakes per upstream. These actions reduced TLS renegotiations and stabilized accept_queue_depth; 5xx rate returned to baseline by 08:55 UTC. Long-term fix: runtime patch to better prioritize existing keepalives over new handshakes during high accept-queue pressure, and change cert-rotation orchestration to stagger operations per shard. Patch merged: runtime PR #2891; deployment scheduled and small canary validated on 2026-03-12.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Engineering to ship runtime handshake-priority patch and monitor for related regressions (owner: SRE)
2) Control-plane to update cert-rotation orchestrator to sequential/staggered mode (owner: Control Plane team, due 2026-03-20)
3) Add a permanent apigw handshake-rate limiter for dedicated pools (owner: API GW team)
4) Postmortem doc and runbook update for heartbeat-flood scenarios (owner: Incident Response)
5) Reach out to Fathom CS with RCA and mitigation steps applied (owner: Customer Success)
6) Consider adding tenant-level early-shed when accept_queue_depth > threshold (owner: Platform Reliability)
7) Monitor dedicated-pool-42 for a week for recurrence and report daily to SRE channel
